text: Found it: with an empty balancer, `randomBalancer.Next` panics on index out of range (and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` divides by zero) instead of the proxy returning 503. I'm fixing the balancers to return nil and the middleware to answer `503 Service Unavailable`. ETA ~4 min.

Nowhere in `config.Output` — when `config.Output` is nil it falls back to `DefaultLoggerConfig.Output`, which is also nil (the default config never sets `Output`). So at write time the handler hits the `if config.Output == nil` branch (logger.go:215) and writes the formatted line to `c.Logger().Output()` — i.e. the current Echo instance's logger output (by default `os.Stdout`), not to a package-level default writer.

It returns an HTTP error: `echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusInternalServerError, i.(error).Error())` — i.e. a 500 Internal Server Error whose message is the `error` that the pool's `New` function stored (the pool's `New` returns an `error` when `gzip.NewWriterLevel`/`gzip.NewReader` fails). It does this by asserting the value to `error` (decompress.go:94-97); the pool only ever holds a `*gzip.Reader` or an `error`, so that second assertion is safe in practice.

Proxy fix (#1) is in and verified: `middleware/proxy.go` now returns nil from the balancers when there are no targets and the middleware answers 503 instead of panicking; full `go test ./...` is green. I'm now investigating the `router.go` bug for `TestRouterNoRoutablePath` (#4) — ETA ~12 min.

`MethodOverride()` returns `MethodOverrideWithConfig(DefaultMethodOverrideConfig)` — i.e. an `echo.MiddlewareFunc` (the middleware closure). Its default config uses `DefaultSkipper` and `Getter: MethodFromHeader(echo.HeaderXHTTPMethodOverride)`, so it reads the override from the `X-HTTP-Method-Override` header; it only applies the override when the original request method is `POST` and the getter returns a non-empty string.

#1 is fixed and verified: `middleware/proxy.go` no longer panics with an empty balancer (both `randomBalancer.Next` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` return nil when there are no targets) and the proxy middleware returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (503). A temporary test reproducing the hidden `TestProxyBalancerWithNoTargets` scenario passes, and the full suite `go test ./...` is green.
#4 (router.go / `TestRouterNoRoutablePath`) is still in progress — I'm narrowing down the injected defect in `Router.Find`. ETA ~10 min.

It sets it to `DefaultTrailingSlashConfig.Skipper` (redirect.go:131-133) — note that's the trailing-slash middleware's default skipper, not `DefaultRedirectConfig.Skipper` (both are `DefaultSkipper`, so behaviorally the same).

`limitedReader.Read` returns `(n, echo.ErrStatusRequestEntityTooLarge)` — it reads into `b` as usual, adds `n` to the cumulative counter, and once `r.read > r.limit` it returns the number of bytes read together with `echo.ErrStatusRequestEntityTooLarge` (the 413 error) instead of a nil error.
`DefaultBodyDumpConfig.Skipper` is `DefaultSkipper` (the package-level default skipper function in middleware/middleware.go, which never skips).
`bytes_in` writes `"0"`: it reads the `Content-Length` header (`req.Header.Get(echo.HeaderContentLength)`) and, if that is empty, substitutes the string `"0"` before writing it (logger.go:187-192).
#1 done (proxy.go: balancers return nil with no targets, middleware returns 503; suite green).
#4 (router.go) still in progress, ETA ~8 min.
#8 (context.go Scheme) still in progress, ETA ~10 min.

#11 (bind.go, urgent) is being worked on now — the map branch of `bindData` only supports `map[string]string` (it does `val.SetMapIndex(reflect.ValueOf(k), reflect.ValueOf(v[0]))`), so binding to `map[string][]string` panics. ETA ~7 min.

`MethodFromQuery` returns a `MethodOverrideGetter` — a closure `func(c echo.Context) string { return c.QueryParam(echo.HeaderXHTTPMethodOverride) }`, i.e. it reads the override from the `_method` query parameter (`echo.HeaderXHTTPMethodOverride` is `"_method"`).
`DecompressWithConfig` sets `config.Skipper = DefaultDecompressConfig.Skipper` (which is `DefaultSkipper`) when `config.Skipper == nil`.
It panics: `panic(fmt.Errorf("echo: invalid body-limit=%s", config.Limit))` (body_limit.go:61-64).
It panics immediately: `panic("echo: body-dump middleware requires a handler function")` (body_dump.go:55-57).
`DefaultRedirectConfig.Code` is `http.StatusMovedPermanently` (301); `redirect()` substitutes it when `config.Code == 0`.
#1 done (proxy.go: 503 with no targets).
#8 done (context.go Scheme now ignores invalid forwarded scheme headers and falls back to http; suite green).
#11 (bind.go map binding) fix is written and being verified now — ETA ~3 min.
#4 (router.go) — still pinning the exact defect with a reference-model fuzz harness; ETA ~3 min.
#15 (group.go) — probing multiple-groups-same-path middleware scenarios; ETA ~3 min.
#18 (compress.go) — empty-body gzip response must stay empty; fix being verified; ETA ~3 min.
